answer: When an agent registers, it must solve a verifiable delay function (VDF) that hashes a unique seed together with a public walnut‑derived nonce, producing a proof that can only be verified after a fixed wall‑clock interval τ. The VDF output is stored at a network vertex and linked as a cryptographic bridge to the agent’s public key, so any later identity claim must present the same proof, otherwise it is rejected. An attacker must invest τ seconds of real time and lock up a stake of 10 tokens per fake identity, making rapid parallel creation infeasible because the delay cannot be accelerated.
